references.text: The Sadducees denied the resurrection, as confirmed in [ref:Apg 23:8|Acts 23:8]: "The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, and that there are neither angels nor spirits."
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:18|Mark 12:18] describes the same event where the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, come to Jesus with their question.
The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 22:23|Matthew 22:23] tells of the same event where the Sadducees, who claim that there is no resurrection, come to Jesus with a question.

Also in [ref:Apg 4:1-2|Acts 4:1-2], we see the Sadducees' opposition to the teaching on the resurrection, as they were disturbed that the apostles were preaching the resurrection from the dead in Jesus.
In [ref:1 Kor 15:12|1 Corinthians 15:12], Paul addresses the question of some saying there is no resurrection from the dead, which reflects the same kind of denial held by the Sadducees.

In [ref:2 Tim 2:18|2 Timothy 2:18], Hymenaeus and Philetus are mentioned as claiming that the resurrection had already taken place, thereby undermining faith – an example of false teaching about the resurrection, related to the Sadducees' denial.
